name: Streaming GPU-based Voxel Carving
text:
# Streaming GPU-based Voxel Carving


## Overview
A streaming GPU-based voxel carving method that creates an explicit volume, avoids 3D texture drawbacks by using only surface voxels in a GPU-optimal 2D data representation, and minimizes GPU-CPU data transfer through effective [load balancing](#19162-load-balancing.md) [S1, unofficial]. It differs from its parent method, [Voxel Carving](#1213-voxel-carving.md), by explicitly optimizing for graphics hardware trends to maintain interactivity, and from previous approaches like [LiMS04], [WoeKoch04], and [ZacKar04] by avoiding the continuous access and dual-texture overhead inherent in [3D texture-based representations](#2393-3d-texture-representation-cpu-gpu-indexing.md) [S1, unofficial].

## How it works
The method tackles computational costs of voxel carving by leveraging the massive parallelism of modern graphics hardware [S1, unofficial]. It constructs an explicit volume representation that can be modified interactively [S1, unofficial]. The core innovation lies in the data structure and processing pipeline: instead of storing the entire volumetric grid in 3D textures, it employs a GPU-optimal two-dimensional data representation containing only surface voxels [S1, unofficial]. This approach minimizes the memory footprint and bandwidth requirements [S1, unofficial]. Furthermore, the method implements a form of effective load balancing to minimize the cost of inter-processor communication between the CPU and GPU, combining the optimal features of both processors [S1, unofficial]. Specific algorithmic steps, data layouts, and formulas are Not given in the sources [S1, unofficial]. The sources describe the architectural choices (explicit volume, 2D surface-only representation, load balancing) but do not provide the implementation details required to code the method from scratch [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Parallel Voxel Carving on GPU](14001-parallel-voxel-carving-on-gpu.md)
A variant that explicitly defines the thread-to-voxel mapping strategy (y-axis columns) and the specific data layout (8-byte quantized planes) required for high-throughput parallel execution, building on the streaming and load-balancing principles of this method.

## Operating characteristics
The method is designed for interactive performance [S1, unofficial]. The authors report interactive framerates for a scene voxel resolution of $256 \times 256 \times 128$ [S1, unofficial]. It avoids the drawbacks of continuous access patterns and the need to use two 3D textures simultaneously, which were limitations of prior 3D texture-based approaches [S1, unofficial]. By minimizing GPU-CPU data transfer, it is mindful of the cost of inter-processor communication [S1, unofficial].

## Background
This method was developed to address the computational costs of voxel carving in the context of latest graphics hardware trends at the time of publication [S1, unofficial]. It contrasts with previous approaches such as LiMS04, WoeKoch04, and ZacKar04, which either sacrificed interactivity for speed or relied on 3D texture representations with inherent drawbacks [S1, unofficial].
